title: Kenoma: Cold Under a Blanket of Stars

items.html: Floors lying down with you, sleeping with you. You roll deeper into their cover and blanket, pulling the sheets until you pull the walls down with them. That isn’t enough, is it? So you pull harder, wanting to steal the blanket from others, and you wrap yourself with the ceiling too. Soon enough, you cover yourself with the stars and vast dark of the night sky. You bend the stars down and wrap yourself with them. Cold, no matter how thick the blanket is. You can’t escape the pain. You have to wake up.

items.html: Each sweep of the cone finds something and loses it. The green-black glint of brass gyroscopes gone soft with verdigris. A tube-screen furred in dust, its glass a dirty moon. A horned phonograph with no needle, a ring of antennas bent like the ribs of a drowned boat, glass jars of coiled filament, a cracked orrery whose planets hang at the wrong ends of their arms, a hundred clocks all disagreeing about the seconds, minutes, and hours. The grease on the dials and the crust on the lenses catch the beam and scatter it, and the walls flicker with reflections that die as soon as the light moves on. It is a hoard kept the way an old aquarian collector keeps a cabinet: everything strange, nothing sorted, all of it loved. On a stone shelf near the back sit crystal lodges, dark and empty, waiting like cups for a drink.

Needles go into the insides of his arms, titrating a fixed chemical fueling unknown. Then the practitioner’s hand, black-gloved and rune-burned to the knuckles, draws one long line down the sternum under the cone of the goggles, and the line fills before the blade has lifted.

items.html: The saw rasps. Bone dust lifts pale into the light and settles on the wet like frost. A grunt cranks the spreader, ratchet after ratchet, and the cage of the chest gives at its seams with a sound like green wood. The chest is cubed out, four clamped corners drawing the meat of the man into a square window, and steam climbs out of the cavity into the cold of the cave, the first warmth it has felt in an age. The surgery runs a day long. Shifts of grunts change and change, the cone bleeds down and is fed again, and the hours countless somewhere, probably on whichever clock correct.

items.html: Inside, the heart waits dark and wet, beating with the patience of a thing asleep. The practitioner clamps the great vessels, one, two, three, and the beat falters, stutters, stops. For a moment the chest holds a silence a little too much. He lifts the heart out in both hands, a fist of dark meat, heavy and dripping on the stone, and sets it in a dish, where it knocks twice against the metal, small and wet, and is still.

items.html: The new heart waits on its tray, ribbed like the tubes on his back, copper gone green, its valve a clenched jaw. Lodged deep in its throat is a crystal the size of a thumb, soul-imbued and dark, inserted in surgery. Black wire goes through the great vessels stitch by stitch, the flesh gathering like a closing mouth, and the blood has to learn the machine’s angles before it will go through them.

items.html: On its ledge the old machine watches with its slit eyes, flaring once, then easing down the way a lamp eases when its oil is spent. A breath of steam leaves the white and broken porcelain mask. The crystal brightens in the new heart, thin at first, then steady, the first light in the cave not borrowed from a lens, and an angel implants himself by a mechanical addition into the man’s heart. The cyber-necronic surgery imbues the two together in severance precision, an operation steady with quiet. A grunt turns the crank. The heart clicks once, twice. The body arches on the slab like andrenaline, with a long vowel of breath and no voice, and the blood finds its way.

items.html: The old husk of that broken porcelain mask can be forgotten now. From the oceans they pulled another, this one missing its wings. His eyes disturbed the scribes and defied their notes, no angel every bearing the eyes of a serpent, with one looking at the room and one past it, and for that reason alone these Euclids listened to his elder instruction.

items.html: He claimed his name at the outset: Antony. The angel spoke of Tartarus, the only angel to have been there and come back; he described it as a nightmare within nightmares, though dreadfully aware, even inside it, of its foreboding falsehood. He had discovered the half of himself, the sleeping-demi-God rising, he said, one he had great pity for but could not help. He watched his destruction countlessly, and felt his boundless suffering as his own, like a father.

items.html: That was before. Now, with the angel lodged in the crystal and the crystal lodged in the heart, the gas is weaned.

items.html: The chosen one begins to awake, looking in confusion, gathering himself in a head rolling left and right in burning perspirations. The room swirls, a reality-ruse lifting. But the swirling does not stop at the edge of the cave. It goes inward, down through the new valves, into the chambers of the heart, where the rooms are made of stone like a long forgotten time.

items.raw: Stars and stone tides before an ocean cast.

items.html: Dreams.
items.raw: Dreams.

items.html: This isn’t him.
items.raw: This isn’t him.

items.html: He stands on a shore he has never seen and has always known, where a tide of stone draws back from the black of an ocean cast. Something sits at the edge of it with its knees drawn up and its face turned towards him, patient as an old lamp. The first beat comes from the far chamber: a ratchet, ticking with clicks that accelerate, an analog tenor warmed. The second answers from the near chamber: a drum, old, hammering, a war’s worth of habit. Neither gives. Every pulse is a vote.

items.html: “Get out of my chest.” It is spoken by him, or thought by him, or said by his throat for him.
items.raw: “Get out of my chest.” It is spoken by him, or thought by him, or said by his throat for him.

items.html: “I am not in it,” the thing answers. “It is in me, and has been since before there was a me to be in.”
items.raw: “I am not in it,” the thing answers. “It is in me, and has been since before there was a me to be in.”

items.html: Then it opens the ocean and lets him look. The moment finds him dead, millions within millions, not of the millions but in them: a boy cornered in a room, a man locked in with a glow, a soldier dragged by the knees through mud, each one drowning, each one his, each one watched. This is the weight the angel carries, twelve eternities of a dark that listens, a head falling past stars and through clouds into a pit of Leviathan, and what held him through all of it was not hope for himself. It was a watching. Every time the sleeper died, the angel saw, and could not reach him.

items.raw: “That isn’t me.”

items.html: “Not anymore,” the thing says. “It was the half of you that chose to sleep. I am the half that watched. Samson.”
items.raw: “Not anymore,” the thing says. “It was the half of you that chose to sleep. I am the half that watched. Samson.”

items.html: Samson thinks him mistaken, even if the gutt agrees.
items.raw: Samson thinks him mistaken, even if the gutt agrees.

items.html: The crystal heats until the new heart blisters the old muscle around it. On the slab the body convulses, the needles shiver in the arms, the grunts lean their weight on the straps in enough time, and the cone of the goggles swings and the whole cave leaps with it. Inside, the seeming contridiction ends the only way it can, out of breath. The ratchet takes a beat from the drum. The drum takes a tick from the ratchet. The heart finds the darkness and beyond, the two swirling together, each for the other’s taking, and keeps one time.

items.html: In the haze of the cave he steadies a now-shaking hand, like someone else’s. Confused.

items.html: “Why do I know?”
items.raw: “Why do I know?”

items.html: After much time, he began to understand how it had all come to this point.
items.raw: After much time, he began to understand how it had all come to this point.

items.html: An angel now in human form, given the power of these Euclids of the South, the tribe of Binah. After a week among the Euclid village, they gave back his tanking form of heavy green armor, and the two of them journeyed out into the mountains, seeking divine insights in their journey.

items.html: They appropriately chose to climb in the daytime, because aggressive wildlife is more plentiful at night. The resistance of the incline was nothing for Samson’s armor, nor was the foliage of the lower part of the mountain they chose. In the in-between of their journey upward, a crimson shroud appeared beneath a tree of death, standing like a tombstone that blotted out the sun.

items.html: Samson and his heavy armor were carried by a curious whisper of life: “Let the sun meet the moon at shade joining, listen if you will.”

items.html: Now, before the tree, Samson grows cold, but his necromantic heart grows warm. The moon hangs in the daylight as a thin crescent, its shadow side large. The crimson shroud glows softly in its own color, burning with a rising dark flame.

items.html: “What?!” Samson sees the flame’s darkness refuse to reflect in his amber visor.
items.raw: “What?!” Samson sees the flame’s darkness refuse to reflect in his amber visor.

items.html: “Trust in the timing of power.” Antony gestures from within the heart-Nous that holds him.
items.raw: “Trust in the timing of power.” Antony gestures from within the heart-Nous that holds him.

items.html: When the dark flame, laced with blood-colored fire, detonates higher, its black trails reach for the sky like an angry outburst. A wind like God almost throws Samson off the cliff. He leans forward, torso low, one leg bent in balanced readiness, and he would be gone if not for the engine firing its cylinder works, pushing him up and away from the edge. The revving roars loud against the battering air-drag, his teeth gritting in suspenseful focus. Armor against wind, cylinder after cylinder, the engine fighting the force plate by plate. Still the heels drag rearward through the dirt, two furrows behind him, and he loses ground slowly, an inch at a time.

items.html: Losing to the air, Samson hears Antony reveal it from within: “We must go into the flame! It is a portal, and it comes once in twenty years!”

items.html: Samson grits his teeth harder, deeper into the gums. The engine’s explosions count upward, the exhaust exhaling red and orange flame, as heat expands and fights the cold air closing around him. Left leg, machine and muscle contracting; right leg, up and closer; the engine working louder. The machine finds its way to the darkest part of the portal as the sun of the sky ignites red. Emptiness and fullness meet.

items.html: Samson is in a stillness now, the engine’s throttle loose, the gears downshifting. He stands under a tree emanating life like a fountain, glowing like the sun from its heart, where the night is now awoken. The moon serves as a stepping stool for a woman’s shadow, who weaves fabrics out of the clouds as creation; her weaving is with claws of a crab on a human shape. A voice speaks from the night, at and into the safety of the tree’s shadow, now made of sun.

items.html: “You will be further free in soul this time, by way of another battle foretold in my soothsayings… Go to the north shores of this island; a serpent awaits in the depthful sea. Revenge is owed to your heart, for myself, and unto the world. It is the pleasure of kōaḥ that you kill the Leviathan, so that his soul will be cast into the outer darkness, a new home for the beast.”

items.html: “Celestialize the heavens with the littering of darkness, littering with a Serpent hated, with the corpse of Leviathan, made true by your thundering lightning and scorching life, both judgements as one are fair in eternity space. Tartarus will celebrate this castration of the dark oceans, which frees both Adam and Eve from the past.” Thus spoke the shadowy woman with crab claws, who stands on the moon.

items.html: The tank before the shore, a standing weight of green iron at the cliff’s edge, where clouds cover the oceans from above, a dark and heavy mist. The air tastes of salt and struck metal; the rain has not come yet, only the cold smell of its coming. The pneuma of the shadowy woman with claws of a crab from the moon blows, her voice heard in the soul by those who can hear, a breath without a mouth. Below, the sea begins to turn: a whirling, spinning and circling, pulling itself inward upon itself, throwing, thrashing, tearing the fish from the dark and shooting them skyward in silver scatters.

items.html: The lowest pitch ever heard quakes up from below, a volcanic sound, elder hatred erupting through the floor of the world. It climbs the armor’s legs, rattles the plates, and settles in the teeth. Cold, fast, the beast slides up and out, and long into the air, the black slick of the abyss pouring from its scales. The serpent lets loose a hissing plurality, every dissonance at once, a choir of dying engines, its teeth taller than any structure that has ever stood near. The clouds unleash a hail of rain, faster and faster with the arrival of the demon, and the storms drown even the ocean. The waves, violently stirred by the spirit of darkness arrived, shoot up and into one another in ways that defy all time.

items.html: Antony, the guardian angel: his form is primordial, made of judgement, time, protection, responsibility, and endurance. His temperament is cold and dry, the patience of old stone, where anger escapes only as a last resort.

items.html: Leviathan: the prime evil form of empty darkness, bondage, hell, exile, and chaos. His temperament is cold and dry, the dead cold of a deep no light has ever touched, a hungry mouth made of grudges.

items.html: Up in order. Samson stands proud in his moment before the orders from the fullness, whereas Antony will release another grudge, long carried, in deserving judgement.

items.html: Samson starts. He matches the speed of the cylinder fires, releasing the clutch, and the drive bites: exhausts spraying flames, torque throwing him forward with intense power. Strides fast, stomps, each footprint’s force cratering the dirt and propelling him onward. He flies.

items.html: The cylinders tighten their beat, the throttle lifts, the clutch cuts, and flames spit from the exhausts as he shifts into another gear; the clutch bites, and he is jerked into another torque. Power rises with each rhythmic acceleration of faster shafts rounding, the engine screaming, then climbing onto another gear, and another, the exhaust heat shooting out from his large heels and wide back. The rain hisses to steam on the plates at the touch. He reaches the cliff’s edge above the shore and launches off it. The machine fires from above the feet and from behind, the jets screaming louder now, his visor covering in dark and grey-blue reflections and the scatters of raindrops.

Its eyes are large and fierce, an emptying blackness of the unknown, wells that have never reflected anything but what they have swallowed. The stretch of the mouth in that scream is enough to devour the world.

items.html: Flying up and into the direction of evil, Samson’s jets propel him into a higher gear, screaming at speeds incomprehensible to any normal vehicle. The suit thrusting still, he looses a long blade from both arms, long of steel and proven. Where he flies into the serpent, into its still-screaming blackness, he slides up its flank, a skyscraper of scale above the storms, the waves crashing below him over some of the jets. Then he lets the engines cut for a little while.

The red blood stands in contrast with the blues and greys, mixing with the water on the amber visor, his face focused in the tunnel that is acceleration.

Something is in the way. He would shake the Earth until she came falling out, just to know.

The armor tumbles end over end, sky and sea and sky, rotating about, the exhaust flaring in spirals, and they plummet in the wrong gear.

The suit lies stuck and immobile in the wet sand, one arm bent wrong, the other pinned beneath its own weight, steam hissing where the hot metal meets the rain.

Broken breaths, thin and whimpering hints of terror behind the joyful exterior always enforced; static in the soul and air; dissonant flutes without tempo or rhythm; a bellowing sea of words without reason; all of it quiet and afar inside a loud closeness that is not here. The space stutters onward toward infinity, jagged with the conformity of itself. The little ones reflect light from nowhere, from a lost source into nothing.

Along the new human back, the shoulder blades split and lift, and the wings reform: the spars first, long and white as the ribs of a drowned ship, then the vanes, then the feathers, one by one, wet, grey at their edges, heavy with storm water. The wings open anew.

He climbs in a long ascension through cloud and thunder, and far below the ocean is a floor of red and black where the serpent thrashes.

The kicks break down and through every twelfth fraction of Leviathan exposed in the ocean, ripping his flesh in localized chunks, spraying blood to mix with the water.

Twelve times did the lightning strike twelve at once, with one hundred and forty-four wounds, plus the lightning that cut his tongue into two permanent halves, even down to his throat.

From the push of a finger through the exterior, Antony reaches effortlessly, his snake-eye glow lighting the wound, and begins a long, long-awaited violence. By forceful digs he ruptures and shreds an opening, a prisoner escaping the walls of twelve of twelve eternities, and the snake’s flesh hides a weapon of his own. Through deeper digging, the viper thrashes with a behemoth cry of its own, the cry of a rabbit in fear.

In blindness he grabs the spine in a death grip, his legs strung out along the axis of the centrifugal. Spun about in confusion still, the light emerges, and he realizes the encircling is bringing his head soon out of the water. The flat top of the water closes near, the pressure loosening, and saltwater and blood run out of his eyes, nose, and ears as he is taken out into air.

The lens caves in crinkling flesh that sprays blood, and the spine is in, vertebra after vertebra, deeper still, as deep as torment, until it can go no further.
